sum est, ea mole & figura quam habet. Inveni au-
tem similem in Anglia ad Ostium Thamisis, aliquan-
diu fluctibus iactatum ita, ut lineæ & striæ minus

page.notes: The woodcut shows an oval stone with eye-like circular markings; it is an illustration, not transcribed as text. Show-through from the facing page is faint at upper right and omitted. The catchword "con-" is treated as the hyphenated line end of the paragraph, and the text runs on to the next page. Some letters in the body are slightly blurred (e.g. "Thamisis", "fluctibus") but read with reasonable confidence.
